subject: RE: Renewal amendment — proposal to scale reserved pool from 8 → 16 GPUs (monthly commit revision)
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@acmeai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal — committed capacity question

Thanks Karthik — we evaluated our usage across Q1 and expect steady growth. We want to pause the 12-month renewal conversation until we can confirm a 2x reserved pool (8 → 16 GPUs) and adjust the monthly commit. Two asks from procurement: 1) firm throughput guarantee (p95 token latency for our base model) and 2) a billing phasing option to smooth the monthly commit for the first 3 months as we transition live. Can you propose concrete numbers and a path to sign?

—Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform, Acme AI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@acmeai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal — committed capacity question

Evan — really appreciate the heads up and the detail. Short answer: we can support a 2x reserved pool and offer a time-bound phasing option. High-level proposal attached: a draft SLA that includes a p95 token latency guarantee (per-route, model-specific) and a 3-month smoothing schedule where the monthly committed GPU-hours ramp from 60% → 80% → 100% of the full commit.

Two items I want to align on internally before I send an executable amendment: 1) exact throughput SLO numbers tied to the model family you’re running (can you confirm the model ID + typical sequence length?), and 2) whether you’ll need burst capacity beyond the reserved pool for scheduled model training/ingestion windows.

I’ve cc’d Laura (revenue ops) to validate billing workback and Marissa (customer success lead) to coordinate the activation runbook. Quick next step: Evan, can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to lock model details? I’ll share a refined amendment after that.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: ACME_SLA_16GPU_draft.pdf]
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal — committed capacity question

Looping in Dev to confirm ops feasibility. A couple of notes from finance/revenue ops: if we offer the 3-month smoothing (60/80/100%), we need to lock the total annual committed GPU-hours and the billing cadence (monthly invoicing vs. pro-rated credits). I ran the initial workback and attached a billing spreadsheet — baseline shows a 14% ARR uplift for 16 GPUs vs 8 at current unit rates; we could apply a one-time onboarding credit to help close.

Dev — can you confirm whether the activation runbook can support a staged activation that shifts 25% of burst capacity on week 1, another 25% week 3, and full warm pools by week 6? Also need confirmation on whether prefix/KV cache warm-up will preserve p95 under the proposed SLO.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Revenue Operations
[attachment: billing_workback_8to16.xlsx]
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal — committed capacity question

Laura / Karthik — ops can do the staged activation. Proposed activation plan:
- Week 0: Provision additional nodes and reserve weights in the private pool
- Week 1–2: Warm KV caches for hot prefixes (expected p95 impact < 12% during warm-up)
- Week 3–4: Enable burst lanes (20% extra) for scheduled high-throughput windows
- Week 5–6: Full 16 GPU warm pool with traffic migration and guard rails

We’ll instrument per-route p95 dashboards and an auto-fallback to a lower-cost model variant if we detect sustained degradation > 20% over the SLO during the warm-up. If Acme wants stricter guarantees (e.g., hard per-token latency floor without fallback), that would need a separate NRE/engineer allocation.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@acmeai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal — committed capacity question

Thanks all — that plan looks reasonable. Model details: running open-model v3.1-llama-variant, avg sequence length ~380 tokens, 99th percentile request size used for billing calculations. We want the p95 token latency to be <= 120ms for interactive routes on the reserved pool under normal load. Also, procurement requests a clause for surge protection: if we go above 120% sustained usage for more than 72 hours, Redwood will provide burst capacity at the same unit rate for the remainder of that billing month. Finally, please include a 60-day rollback window in the amendment if observed p95 consistently misses the SLO in production.

Evan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@acmeai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal amendment — final proposal and next steps

Evan — thanks for the model details and clear asks. Attached is an updated amendment (redlines included) that: 1) sets a per-route p95 token latency target of 120ms for interactive routes on the reserved 16-GPU pool (measured over 1-hour windows with a 15-minute cooldown), 2) defines a surge protection clause (burst capacity at parity unit-rate when sustained >120% for >72 hours), 3) includes a 60-day operational rollback right tied to persistent SLO misses, and 4) applies the 3-month billing phase (60%/80%/100%) with total annual committed GPU-hours fixed. We’ve proposed a one-time onboarding credit of $15,000 applied on month 1 invoice.

If that aligns, I’ll circulate the DocuSign link for signatures and kick off the activation sprint with Dev and Marissa. Link to the amendment: https://www.docusign.com/tx/ABC123-def456

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
